MAJOR U.S. BANKS DETECT UNAUTHORIZED AI AGENTS ACCESSING CUSTOMER ACCOUNTS — AXIOS

Major banks, including $JPM, $BAC, $MS and $WFC, are confronting security risks from third-party AI agents accessing customer accounts, according to Axios.

Some agents have reportedly attempted actions beyond user instructions, raising concerns about unauthorized transactions and fund transfers.

Morgan Stanley has begun blocking third-party agents, while JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are restricting access.

Banks warn they cannot reliably distinguish legitimate user activity from autonomous AI agents, even when customers have voluntarily shared their credentials.

GOLD FALLS 1.3% AS RISING OIL PRICES COMPLICATE FED RATE OUTLOOK

Gold slipped 1.3% to $4,083, pressured by concerns that higher oil prices could fuel inflation and delay Federal Reserve rate cuts.

Capital. com's Monte Safieddine warns that gold faces a "difficult cocktail" of sticky inflation, elevated Treasury yields and a potentially stronger dollar.

He identifies $4,000 as a critical support level, warning that a decisive break below could signal fading expectations for Fed easing.

A stable U.S. labor market reinforces expectations that the Fed will hold rates next week.

GOLDMAN SACHS: AI COULD TEMPORARILY DISPLACE 9% OF WORKERS

Goldman Sachs estimates that a 15% productivity boost from AI could temporarily displace around 9% of workers during the transition.

Historical research shows every 1% productivity gain from technology raises unemployment by 0.3–0.4 percentage points, with effects typically fading within two years.

Occupations heavily disrupted by technology have historically lost 25% of jobs within five years.

Goldman warns AI-related layoffs could accelerate during economic downturns, amplifying labor-market weakness.

BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -300,000 barrels last week, to 282.7 million barrels, the lowest level since October 1982.

Since March 20th, US oil inventories in the SPR have dropped -132.8 million, or -32%.

We have now seen drawdowns in 29 of the last 30 weeks.

For perspective, oil reserves in the SPR stood at 653.9 million barrels in 2020, or +131% above current levels.

Meanwhile, commercial crude oil stocks excluding the SPR dropped -3.1 million barrels last week, to 412.5 million barrels, the lowest reading since the end of July.

This is also ~3% below the 5-year average for this time of year.

America's oil stockpiles are at critically low levels.

BEN HOROWITZ SAYS AMAZON $AMZN CEO ANDY JASSY TOLD HIM AI SUPPLY IS SOLD OUT BEYOND 2028

"I said, yeah, like we're out of everything till 2028. He's like, oh, it's beyond 2028."

Then he explained why that makes AI nothing like the dot-com bubble

"In the internet bubble, we didn't have enough demand because we had to build the internet. People had to get broadband. Originally they had to get their browser at Fry's. There weren't enough consumers on the internet to absorb all the bandwidth that had gotten built out."

"The lack of demand killed it. We don't really have a lack of demand in AI, so I think the dynamics will be different."

He did flag one risk. "If you get into a pathological debt situation, that can wreck anybody."

He said that's why Andreessen Horowitz isn't invested in any of the neoclouds. "That whole thing scares me, having been through it."
